recipe_version.title: Sichuan Mapo Tofu with Shiitake and Jasmine Rice
recipe_version.description: Soft tofu cubes simmered in a glossy, numbing-hot sauce of broad bean chili paste, fermented black beans, garlic, ginger, and toasted Sichuan peppercorn, with finely chopped shiitake for a meaty bite. Served over jasmine rice with scallions.

ingredients.name: Sichuan broad bean chili paste (doubanjiang)
ingredients.display_name: Sichuan broad bean chili paste (doubanjiang) whose label lists broad beans, chiles, salt, and wheat flour, with no shrimp or fish

ingredients.name: Sichuan chili flakes or crushed red pepper
ingredients.display_name: Sichuan chili flakes or crushed red pepper

ingredients.name: scallions
ingredients.preparation: thinly sliced, whites and greens separated

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Rinse the rice until the rinse runs nearly clear. Cut the tofu into 3/4-inch cubes. Stem the shiitake and chop the caps finely. Mince the garlic and ginger, rinse and chop the black beans, and slice the scallions, keeping whites and greens apart. In a small bowl stir the cornstarch into 3 tbsp water.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.body: Combine the rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and 1/2 tsp salt in a 2-quart saucepan. Bring to a boil over high, about 4 minutes, then cover, turn to low, and cook 15 minutes; leave it covered off the heat to rest 10 minutes. The covered cooking and rest run inside steps 3 to 7 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Toast the peppercorns
steps.body: Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry 12-inch skillet over medium-low, shaking the pan, until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Tip them into a mortar or spice grinder and grind coarsely.

steps.title: Brown the shiitake
steps.body: Heat the oil in the same skillet over medium-high. Add the chopped shiitake and cook, stirring often, until browned and no longer wet, about 7 minutes.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.body: Turn the heat to medium. Stir in the doubanjiang and cook until the oil turns red, about 1 minute. Add the garlic, ginger, black beans, scallion whites, and chili flakes and stir 1 minute. Add 1 cup water, the soy sauce, and the sugar and bring to a simmer, about 1 minute.

steps.title: Simmer the tofu
steps.body: Slide in the tofu and gently push it with the back of a spoon so it is coated without breaking. Simmer, spooning the sauce over, until the tofu is hot through, about 6 minutes.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.body: Stir the slurry (the cornstarch and 3 tbsp water) and pour it in thirds, nudging the tofu between additions, until the sauce turns glossy and coats a spoon, about 1 minute. Sprinkle in half the ground peppercorn.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Fluff the rice and spoon it into wide bowls. Spoon the mapo tofu alongside and finish with the remaining ground peppercorn and the scallion greens.

equipment: mortar and pestle or spice grinder

coverage_contribution: A plant-based HH001 tofu dinner in a sauce-over-rice format. Sichuan flavor (chili bean paste, numbing peppercorn) is represented live only by a dry green bean stir-fry. Tofu leads are tacos, teriyaki bowls, a red curry, and a Korean stew; none is a thickened chili-bean sauce.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with korean-soft-tofu-stew: a thick chili-bean sauce spooned over rice, not a brothy gochugaru stew with egg. Compared with sichuan-green-bean-mushroom-stir-fry: soft tofu simmered and thickened in sauce, not dry-fried beans. Compared with teriyaki-tofu-bowls: soft tofu in fermented chili bean sauce, not seared tofu in a sweet glaze. Compared with taiwanese-three-cup-mushrooms: doubanjiang and Sichuan peppercorn, no basil, rice wine, or sesame oil.
not_duplicate_of: Not a pork mapo; the shiitake version keeps it HH001.
